• Common name: Pogostemon helferi
  • Other names: Dao-noi or Little star
  • Minimum tank size: 10 gallons (~40 liters)
  • Difficulty: Medium to hard
  • Lighting: Moderate to high
  • Optimal pH: 6.0 – 8.0
  • Optimal hardness: Moderately hard water
  • Optimal temperature: 22 – 26 °C (72 – 77 °F)
  • Substrate: Needed (nutrient-rich)
  • Can float: No
  • Can be grown emersed: Yes
  • Size: 7 – 15 cm (3 – 6 inches)
  • Growth form: Stem
  • Growth rate: Slow to moderate (submersed), moderate (emersed)
  • Placement in tank: Foreground / midground
  • Fertilizer: Needed
  • CO2: Needed
  • Propagation: Cutting, lateral shoots, and seed (emersed)
Pogostemon helferi has a limited distribution range. This plant can only be found across Myanmar and western Thailand.
In its natural habitat, Pogostemon helferi often grows emersed or submerged along the banks of rivers and streams. That makes this plant also a good choice for paludarium setups.

Pogostemon helferi is a demanding plant and not good for beginners since it requires almost ideal conditions. Even under optimal conditions, growth is only moderate at best, so it will not overrun the tank if left unattended for some time.

  • Pruning: cutting down old leaves is one of the significant methods of caring for this plant.
  • Do not let other plants overshadow it; this is a sure way to kill it.
  • Partial water changes are crucial since they add microelements (nutrition) to the water and improve the growth rate.

Planting

It suits the foreground and midground of planted tanks due to its small size and bushy appearance. Place specimens into a substrate 5 – 7 cm (2 – 3 inches) thick to avoid difficulty in rooting. Keep a spacing of about 5 cm (2 inches) between plants to reduce competition at the early stage and let plantlets establish. Do not plant too tightly, as dense groupings seem to hinder it.

Propagation

  • Seeds (only when grown emersed)
  • Lateral shoots (near the base of the stem)
  • Head cutting of mature stems (possible but not recommended)

Because of its small size, head cutting is not the best method, though pruning the tops promotes side shoots and makes plants denser. In aquariums, lateral shoots are the main way of propagation: cut them right at the base so each has a crown and a few roots. Although it can form an impressive carpet, it is not considered a classical carpeting plant.

Dry Start Method

The Dry Start Method (DSM) provides unlimited CO2 and a lot of light, significantly boosts slow-growing plants, cycles the substrate, and removes algae problems. Pogostemon helferi becomes less picky when grown emersed.

  • Instead of filling the tank with water after planting, add only enough water to reach the surface of the lowest part of the substrate.
  • Cultivate the stems in a nutrient-rich substrate.
  • Spray water regularly to provide high humidity (around 80%).
  • Cover the top of the tank with cling wrap to maintain humidity.
  • Fill the tank with water when the plant's growth kicks off.

Pogostemon helferi is not ideal for beginners due to its high light, CO2, nutrient demands, and stable water parameters. It is sensitive to temperature fluctuations and water quality, so a cycled and fully established tank is very important.

Tank size: a minimum of 10 gallons (~40 L). It can be used sparingly in smaller nano tanks, but this is not recommended because it requires stable water parameters, which are very hard to achieve in small tanks. A larger tank is always preferable for the stability of water chemistry.

Temperature: ideally 22 – 26 °C (72 – 77 °F). Some sources say it tolerates 15 – 28 °C (60 – 82 °F), but such changes must occur very slowly (over several days). Any sudden swing in temperature will cause it to melt.

pH: 6.0 – 8.0.

Hardness: adaptable to a range of values, but grows best at 6 – 18 GH. It does not like soft water. Ideally the water parameters the plant is accustomed to should be known, because a transition from soft to hard water or vice versa will melt the plant.

Water chemistry in the wild: laboratory analysis of water in Kanchanaburi province, Thailand: pH 7.8, conductivity 210 µS, bicarbonate 132 ppm, nitrate (N) 0 ppm, phosphate (P) < 0.14 ppm, potassium (K) < 0.34 ppm, magnesium (Mg) 3 ppm, boron (B) < 0.01 ppm.

Lighting: submersed Pogostemon helferi needs good lighting to keep a robust appearance. Provide medium-high lighting (30-50 PAR) with an efficient lighting system and a photoperiod of at least 8 hours daily (absolute minimum); 10 hours is preferable. Under low light, in the best case it grows thin and its shoots turn yellow-green; usually it melts due to inadequate light or shading by taller plants.

Substrate: when grown submerged it needs a nutrient-rich substrate; it is a heavy feeder with a strong root system. Enriched aqua soils suffice and help develop thicker stems and healthy, fleshy foliage. Recommended: ADA Amazonia aqua soil, Carib Sea Eco-Complete, Seachem Fluorite. Emersed plants can even grow on rocks and driftwood.

Flow: it does not like stationary water. In nature it is found in fast-flowing rivers and streams, and its short, compact rosettes and undulated leaves are well adapted to rapid water. Lack of flow will make it melt within days.

CO2: CO2 injection is a necessity. The plant requires stable CO2 levels to stay healthy and grow densely, so a pressurized CO2 system is better. In low-tech tanks without CO2 it looks flaccid, leggy and stretched, and grows very slowly and not compact.

Fertilization: like any plant it benefits from macro and micronutrients, which sustain healthy growth and best coloration. However, excessive nutrients also suppress growth; nitrates and phosphates are very low in its natural water.

Pogostemon helferi is an ornamental aquatic stem plant (on average 7 to 15 cm tall) characterized by a bushy appearance, compact growth, curly leaves, and bright green coloration.

The leaves are rippled (zig-zag shaped) and curved slightly downward. Although they look very soft and airy, they are quite fragile. Leaf veins are clearly visible; the foliage is smooth and well-formed with no marked distortion, serration, or discoloration.

It can be grown emersed or submersed. In open aquariums, where it grows above the surface, it forms light purple flowers, and it grows faster than the submerged form.

There is also a variation called Pogostemon helferi red, with reddish veins and leaves of a different shade of green with a red tint.

Problems

  • Melting: there are many reasons it can suddenly melt. When an emersed-grown plant is cultivated submerged, the initial leaves melt/die off to make way for new leaves, and growth then continues. Unstable water parameters, low lighting, overshadowing, too little or too much fertilization, and an inappropriate substrate can also cause melting. If the plant is moved and conditions change suddenly, the leaves will melt and new leaves adapted to the new conditions may grow.
  • Fragile: the leaves break very easily during maintenance. Solution: handle the plant with extra care.
  • Hard to plant: young stems are easily damaged and at first lack well-developed roots, so they may float away. Solution: plant with aquarium tweezers and place some pebbles or rocks around the stem, taking care not to damage the stem or roots.
  • Palatable: the fine leaves may be eaten by some snails and fish. Solution: research beforehand.

Benefits

  • Aquascape: an excellent decorative addition to Dutch style aquascapes.
  • No overshadowing: it does not grow big, so it will not block light unlike many tall and/or floating plants.
  • Hiding place for fish, fry, and shrimp: it provides cover and shade for invertebrates, small frogs, and fish.
  • Foraging place: it acts as a buffet of biofilm, an ideal first food for newly hatched fry and baby shrimp.

Compatible tankmates

Pogostemon helferi is compatible with a wide variety of freshwater fish and invertebrates:

  • Fish (for example, Bettas, Swordtails, Tetras, Harlequin Rasbora, Zebra Danios, Clown Killifish, Cherry Barbs, Panda Garra, Albino Bristlenose Pleco, Platies, Guppies, Endlers, Mollies, Otocinclus Catfish, Pygmy Cory Catfish, etc.)
  • Dwarf shrimp such as Neocaridina species (Red Cherry, Blue Velvet, Snowball, Black Rose, Orange Sakura, Green Jade, Rili, etc.) or Caridina species (Crystal Red, Caridina cf. babaulti, Blue Tiger, etc.), Amano shrimp, Ghost shrimp, Bamboo shrimp, Vampire shrimp. Basically, any shrimp species can be kept with it.
  • Freshwater snails (Japanese trapdoor snails, Ramshorn snails, Nerite snails, Malaysian Trumpet snails, Black Devil Snails, Asolene spixi, Rabbit Snails, etc.).

Avoid or be careful

Never keep Pogostemon helferi with crayfish or freshwater crabs, because they will most likely tear up the foliage and uproot the plant.

Also avoid hostile and aggressive fish known as plant devourers, including Texas cichlids, Front cichlids, Jack Dempsey, Red Devil, and Oscars. Angelfish can also uproot and nibble at it, and mystery snails may munch on the leaves.

In conclusion

Pogostemon helferi is a Thai indigenous aquatic plant that is great for the foreground. It has a very unique leaf structure and easily becomes a focal point. It either dies rather quickly or thrives in the tank, with nothing in between. It will struggle in a low-tech tank due to its strong need for intense lighting and CO2 supplementation, and it also needs water flow and nutrient-rich substrates.

  • Christensen C, Andersen T, Pedersen O. (2008a) Hunting for Pogostemon helferi. The Aquatic Gardener 21: 31-41.
